intro: A scatterplot you can change. Drag any point, or tap empty space to add one, and the least-squares line, r, r², s and the residual plot are recomputed from the points on the screen.
howItWorks:
The least-squares line ŷ = a + bx has slope b = r · sy / sx and passes through (x̄, ȳ), so a = ȳ − b x̄. It is the one line that makes the sum of the squared residuals as small as possible. A residual is actual minus predicted, y − ŷ. The standard deviation of the residuals is s = √(Σ residual² / (n − 2)).

Flags use stated rules of thumb: an outlier has |residual| more than 2s, high leverage means x more than 2 standard deviations from x̄, and a point is influential when removing it changes the slope by more than 20% or r by more than 0.1.
